cells.place: Superintendent of Research and Museums, Bhubaneswar. Through Dr. D. C. Sircar.
cells.remarks: Records that from Mādhavapura the king granted the village of Tamaḍāṭa situated in Vyāghrapurabhukti of Jayapura-viṣaya to 24 Brāhmaṇas. Guhachandra served as the executor of the grant and Upēndrasimā, son of Kuṇḍa-chandra, was the dūtaka. The document was composed and engraved the document and Peṭṭapāla Jyeṣṭhasimha affixed the seal. Published in the Journal of the Kalinga Historical Research Society, Vol. II, No. 1, p. 65 ff., and Ep. Ind., Vol. XXX, pp. 148 ff.

cells.location: NELLORE DISTRICT — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: concld. Nellore Taluk—concld. Nollūru—Vēṇugōpālasvāmin temple in Mūlapēṭa. Right of entrance into the main shrine.
cells.date: Śaka 1828, Viśvāva. Kārttika śu. 13, Thursday, Irogu-lar.
cells.remarks: States that Śrī-Nārāyaṇa-Rāmānuja-Jīyar of the Yadugiri-Yatirāja-maṭha of Melukōṭe, belonging to the Vaikhā-na-sa-rājya in Karṇāṭa-maṇḍala, established by Śrī Rāmā-nujāchārya, on his pilgrimage to Badarikā-śrama in the north, having camped at Nollūru alias Nellūru, arranged for a Vaikhānasāgama-sampradāya-pūjā in Mūlathānēśvarapēṭa (Mūlapēṭa) and established certain practices according to the pāñcharātra-āgama in the temple after the pathi-patrika of Rāmānuja Jīyar, the fourth pontiff after the former, visited the place being on a pilgrimage to the north in the Śaka year 1847, Raktākshin, Vaiśākha śu. 1, Sunday, received the honours due to him from the maṭha officials there and presented the record and the record-ing of this inscription on stone. The signatures of the Dharmakartas are appended below the inscription.

cells.remarks: Fragmentary and built in. Seems to refer to some gift of land made to the temple of god Aḍikallīśvara. Cf. Inscriptions of the Nellore District, p. 818, No.50.

cells.remarks: In modern characters. Refers to the ancient history of a Jain Chaitya constructed at Bhadrādipura by the merchant Dēvachandra who also installed an image of Pārśvanātha. Refers to a great famine that occurred in the year V. S. 1315 and caused the depopulation of the city of Bhadrādipura which was again made habitable by the financial aid rendered by the Jain merchant Vimalachandra. Also records a donation of 50,000 drammas by Mahārājādhirāja for the spread of the Jaina religion. Mentions two ladies Vīrabāyī and Mīṭhabāyī.

cells.remarks: In two fragments. Contains several panels with representa- tions of deities, mostly female, in a few cases both male and female and in rare cases only male. Two lines of writing above these figures have been too faint a copy to decipher. They seem to read 1. ... Vīrōchāvaḍaṁ nāśa(i)yuti yuti 75,000... ka vu(bu)ddhīvaṁ paravāyā-chchhēdanaṁ 2... jalastambhanaṁ... etc. and ending with a-kṣaya-nīvī-raksha-bhāra-dharmma. Below the representations of deities which are numbered are engraved names such as Rājāvaṭadēvī, Nimāvaṭadēvī, Pratī-rūpadēvī, Sīmantinīdēvī, Lōlamadēvī, Bhūtīśvarīdēvī, Oṁkāradēvī, Bhūtīśvarīdēvī, Dēvī-rūpā and Kṣēmavāṭī. In characters of about the 12th century.

cells.location: Rāmpurā
cells.place: Do. Stone built into Pādāhārī Bavdī.
cells.remarks: Records the praśasti of Durgabhāṇ, son of Pratāpa and father of Chandra belonging to the lunar race and states that out of the excessive zeal for charitable and pious deeds he performed other meritorious acts. The tank was excavated by mahārā- jadhīra Rāmadāsa. The praśasti was composed by Kēśava of Bhāradvāja-gōtra. Mentions a jinālaya and about the end of the record one Saugata-dharma-vētā.

cells.location: Mangrol
cells.place: Do. Do., No. 2, originally from the Gādī Gate.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. States that, when Malik Ya‘qūb of Tamīn origin was in charge of the shiq of Sorath, on behalf of Zafar Khān, the governor of the province, at a time when the fort of the city of Surat, the work of making the rings and loops of the gates of the strong and high city-wall of Manglore in steel and iron was carried out at the instance of the Sultan, by his brother Malik Mūsa, the son of the former. Two hundred mans of iron is said to have been required for the purpose. Text by Badr, son of Zahīr. For the Sanskrit portion, see No. 513 of Appendix B (ibid., p. 17).

cells.remarks: States that the town of Manglore, which was originally conquered by Sayyid Sikandar, came to be occupied by the infidels of that village, living in the revelance of such tyranny for a period of twelve years. cells.remarks: Records the demise, at the age of 90, of a certain noble, Ahmad Shah, who, it is stated, at one time belonged to the Suhrawardi order. cells.place: Tomb of Wazīr Shāh. Slab fixed into the west wall.
cells.date: A.H. 811, Rabī‘ I 27=1408 A. D. August 20.
cells.language: Persian and Sanskrit, Naskh and Nāgarī.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. Records the construction of the city-wall and a house (guard-room) by Malik Faḍlu’llāh Aḥmad Abū Rajā, the work having started in the reign of Khān-i-A‘ẓam, Zafar Khān, in the reign of Sulṭān Muẓaffar Shāh, son of Muẓaffar Shāh, the king, on Shawwāl 14, A.H. 810, and completed on the given date. For the Sanskritic portion see no. 521 of Appendix B.

BANARAS DISTRICT
Banaras.—Headstone of the grave of Shaikh ‘Alī Ḥazīn. Estampage from the Superintendent, Department of Archaeology, Mid-Eastern Circle, Patna.
cells.remarks: Records the demise of Muḥammad, called ‘Alī, son of Ṭālib al-Jīlānī. Also gives three of his verses wherein the nom-de-plume Ḥazīn is given. No date.
